name: Airtable
look: White canvas with no atmospherics, a near-black and outline button pair, and full-bleed signature colour cards between resets.

hero.title: The database your team can actually use
hero.sub: A spreadsheet people already understand, on top of a real relational database, with interfaces and automations for everyone who should not be looking at the raw grid.

features.title: A grid, then everything above it
features.sub: The grid is the honest part. Interfaces, automations and forms are the parts everyone else uses.

items.title: Relational grids
items.body: Linked records, rollups and lookups — a real relational model behind a familiar grid.

items.title: Interfaces
items.body: Purpose-built screens for the people who should never see the raw table.

items.title: Automations
items.body: Trigger on a record change and run steps, with a run history you can inspect.

items.title: Forms
items.body: Collect structured input straight into the base with validation that actually holds.

items.title: Permissions
items.body: Per-table and per-field access, so finance sees salary and the intern does not.

items.title: Sync and extend
items.body: Two-way sync with your other systems, plus a scripting block for the rest.

showcases.title: The grid is for the owner, not everyone
showcases.body: Most people should never see the base. Interfaces give them a screen built for their job — a queue, a form, a dashboard — while the owner keeps the grid underneath.
points: One source of data behind all of them

showcases.title: Governed, not shadow IT
showcases.body: Spreadsheets sprawl because nobody can see them. Admin controls surface every base in the organisation, who can reach it, and where the data goes.

gallery.title: TEMPLATES
gallery.sub: Start from something someone has already made work.

testimonial.quote: Our ops lead built the whole vendor pipeline herself. Engineering's only involvement was pointing at the sync docs once.
testimonial.name: Simone Barrett

pricing.title: PRICING
pricing.sub: Free for small bases. Priced per editing seat.

items.a: Yes — linked records, referential integrity, rollups and lookups. It presents as a grid because that is what makes it usable, not because it is a spreadsheet underneath.

items.q: Do read-only users cost a seat?
items.a: No. You pay for editors. Interface users and commenters do not consume a paid seat, which is what makes rolling it out across a company affordable.

items.q: Can I get my data out?
items.a: CSV per table, or the API for a full structured export including relations. There is no export fee and no notice period.

items.q: What happens at the record limit?
items.a: You are warned well before, and the base stays readable rather than locking. Upgrading raises the limit immediately.

cta.title: Build your first base
cta.sub: Free to start, no card, and interfaces included from the beginning.

footer.tagline: The database your team can actually use.

notes: The hero is a plain white canvas — no gradient, no mesh, no flourish. The strength comes from type and buttons in clean whitespace.
The signature button pair is a near-black filled CTA beside a canvas-coloured outline button. They travel together.
Brand voltage lives in full-bleed signature colour cards — coral, forest, dark navy — appearing every few screens.
Demo grids sit on warm pastel surfaces: peach, mint and cream carrying product UI fragments.
The canvas resets to white between every signature surface. That reset is what keeps the colour cards from becoming noise.
